title: Continue a long line
objective: Split a long statement across lines so it stays easy to read.

body.text: A statement can be split across lines. If a line ends with a word that needs more to finish it, such as plus, divided by or to, Lagom reads the next line as part of the same statement. Indent the continued line four spaces so it is clear it belongs to the line above.

body.title: Continue after plus
body.code:
make name equal to "Ada"
make greeting equal to "Hello, " plus
    name
say greeting

body.text: A long calculation can continue again and again. Put the operator at the end of each line, so the reader sees that the expression goes on.

body.title: Several continued lines
body.code:
make first equal to 2
make second equal to 2
make third equal to 3
make total equal to first plus second plus
    third
say total

body.text: Split a line only where the statement is not finished yet. A complete line such as say total cannot be continued, so the next line starts a new statement.

body.title: Continue after divided by
body.code:
make total equal to 20
make count equal to 4
make average equal to total divided by
    count
say average

body.prompt: The last line is too long and breaks the indentation rule, so the program stops with a problem. Break it across lines, keeping every continuation line indented four spaces, so it still prints 6.
body.starter:
make first equal to 1
make second equal to 2
make third equal to 3
make total equal to first plus second plus third
say total
body.solution:
make first equal to 1
make second equal to 2
make third equal to 3
make total equal to first plus second plus
    third
say total

checks.description: The line ends with plus, and third is on the next line
